texts.facts: The Tribunal has awarded compensation in MVC No.509/16 against which the Insurance Company has filed MFA No.3421/2017 contending that claimant Nos. 5 and 6 are married daughters of deceased Ramaiah and thus, the - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:16193 Tribunal has erred in awarding compensation to them under `loss of estate' applying the multiplier system as in the case of loss of dependency at Rs.3,50,000/-. As a result, Ganesh, Ramaiah and Master Manoj fell down and sustained grievous injuries. But, the doctors declared Ganesh and Ramaiah brought dead and given - 14 - NC: 2024:KHC:16193 treatment to Master Manoj who sustained injuries in the accident. 9. The claimants filed petitions under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 on the ground that the claimant nos.5 and 6 are none other than the daughters of deceased Ramaiah and the claimants in MVC No.510/2016 contended that claimant no.1 is wife of Ganesh, claimant nos. 2 and 3 are his daughters and claimant no.4 is the son of Ganesh. 10. Therefore, the Tribunal has granted fair and reasonable compensation of Rs.1,00.000/- as global compensation to the injured in this case.
texts.arguments: The rider of the motor cycle knew that he was riding Bajaj Chetak Scooter which was involved in the accident which is meant only for two adults and in extreme circumstances, a child could be accommodated. Considering the capacity of the vehicle, three grown up adults could not have traveled on Bajaj Chetak Scooter. That itself is sufficient ground for cause of accident. When somebody is traveling on a small vehicle with more number of persons, that itself is a detriment to the rider to ride the vehicle smoothly by following all the traffic rules. Therefore, in the fact situation, when the rider of the motorcycle has taken responsibility of taking two pillion riders on such a small vehicle, the rider of the vehicle should have been more cautious - 17 - NC: 2024:KHC:16193 in riding the motor cycle. It is needless to say that the accident took place in such a way that all the three persons on the scooter were grievously injured and out of them two were succumbed to the injuries. 16. Further, it is contended that, the very rash and negligent act on the part of the rider of the motorcycle itself is an offence which is punishable under the provisions of MV Act, inasmuch as, more than two persons travelling on the motorcycle, not being permissible. Learned counsel for the claimant contended that the claimant sustained two grievous injuries and there is fracture of shaft of femur.
